summary: A 2D diffusion sampler. A cloud of random noise is denoised step by step into a target shape (or one the visitor draws), using the exact score of the noised data. A second panel shows the forward noising process at the same noise level.
use_for: generative models, diffusion models, score matching, denoising, GANs, VAEs, normalizing flows, sampling, image generation, density estimation

stochastic.help: true = stochastic (DDPM-style) sampler, false = deterministic ODE sampler

one_liner: Watch random noise get denoised step by step into a shape, then draw your own target.
mechanism: The demo shows the generative half of the story on 2D points. It starts from pure noise and repeatedly takes a small step toward where the data is likely, adding a little fresh noise each time. Below, it runs the forward direction: real data getting noisier, the process the model learns to undo.
try: Press Sample and scrub the timestep slider. The cloud has no structure at high noise, a blurry outline appears in the middle steps, and sharp detail arrives only at the very end.
Change the shape, or drag on the left panel to draw your own target points. Then sample again.
Cut the number of denoising steps to 5. With too few steps the samples come out smeared, which is why fast sampling is an active research problem.
Toggle stochastic off. The deterministic sampler follows smooth paths and gives the same output from the same noise.
simplifications: Instead of a trained neural network, the denoiser here is the exact score of the noised training points. A real model has to learn that function from data, and it generalises instead of memorising points.
The data are a few hundred 2D points, not images. The noise schedule is a simple geometric sequence of noise levels (variance-exploding), chosen so every step is visible.
